mods.name: MMD OreSpawn
mods.description: Configurable, provider-driven terrain, ore, and deposit generation.

releases.notes:
Version 4.1.7.115021

* Add chunk surveys, rule explanations and guarded clear/undo tools with clickable previews.
* Keep completed retrogen revisions through repeated saves, OFF/ON changes and server restarts.
* Add optional natural rock formations and preserve edited provider templates.
* Keep native aquatic decoration working with custom background fluids; preserve later lakes and springs.
* Preserve imported ore settings, avoid duplicate provider defaults and list vanilla Ore Sources with management off.
* Keep saved ore settings when a provider renames a recognised rule. Add the
  matching modern rule as a disabled alternative rather than another ore pass.
* Refresh release checksums when jars change and keep Eclipse launches production-only.

Version 4.1.1.115021

* Fixed a crash when opening or editing OreSpawn's settings in development runs.
  The fix has also been checked in a normal Forge installation.

Version 4.1.0.115021

* Add a directory for loaded provider mods and optional add-on settings screens.
* Group OreSpawn-managed ores by exact block tags. Balanced, Single, Custom,
  and Keep Original policies keep one placement budget per channel without
  changing existing worlds' saved behaviour.
* Add a biome directory with exact new-terrain replacement, palette settings,
  and dimension-wide materials controls. Existing chunks are never rewritten.
* Preserve missing-mod settings and dormant imported Ore Dictionary aliases.
  Provider, global, and world schemas are now 5, 8, and 7; API major remains 1.
* Resolve tag-only ore and fluid hosts after datapack loading and before spawn
  generation, without rebuilding working block or rock-family host rules.
* Reject invalid Geome IDs without silently renaming them. Give Eclipse a
  separate shared-ore test launch and use processed resources after rebuilds.

Version 4.0.16.115021

* Adopt the shared 4.0.16 release identity. Forge 1.15 has no server-side
  GameTest harness, so the later GameTest lifecycle repair is not applicable
  on this target.
* Ordinary dedicated benchmark servers continue to stop automatically when
  requested.

Version 4.0.15.115021

* Classify generated geology and public geology samples through the same
  stable quart-biome cell at three-dimensional biome boundaries.
* Keep ore family-host filters and sampler predictions consistent when later
  surface features alter the final heightmap by a small amount.
* Existing chunks, profiles, API signatures, and schemas are unchanged.

Version 4.0.14.115021

* Convert exposed one-layer vanilla Snow from the first free cell immediately
  above Minecraft's motion-blocking surface when a dimension supplies a custom
  snow material.
* Retain the existing surface Ice conversion and leave buried or authored Snow
  and Ice unchanged.

Version 4.0.13.115021

* Give the public ore-dimension builder the exact biome include/exclude and
  biome-dictionary filter support already available in provider JSON.
* Accept valid namespaced geome IDs in both creation-editor validation paths
  while preserving legacy unnamespaced geome keys.
* API major 1, schemas, existing profiles, generated chunks, and worldgen
  behaviour are unchanged.

Version 4.0.12.115021

* Classify public geology samples at the same highest occupied block used by
  chunk geology generation, rather than the first free block above it.
* Keep public sampler predictions consistent with generated rock at vertical
  biome seams without changing existing chunks, profiles, or generation.

Version 4.0.10.115021

* Evaluate Stable Layers rock min_y and max_y bounds against actual world Y
  instead of the vertically shifted formation coordinate.
* Preserve the shifted formation identity for layer, family, and rock choice
  while preventing vanilla Stone fallback near dimension floors and ceilings.
* Apply the correction only while generating new chunks; existing chunks and
  saved profiles remain unchanged.

OreSpawn 4.1.7.111021
- Add chunk surveys, rule explanations and guarded clear/undo tools for test worlds.
- Keep clear and undo previews valid when protected leaves finish a normal decay check.
- Add optional geological formations and preserve provider template overrides.
- Keep formations out of native structure areas, including woodland mansions.
- Keep completed retrogen revisions through repeated saves and server restarts.
- Retain saved ore rules without enabling duplicate provider defaults.

## 4.1.6.111021

- Fix duplicate ore generation when an OreSpawn 1 world is moved without its converted provider file. Keep imported rules and saved choices, and back up the profile before removing a duplicate. Leave edited rules for review.
- Pick the default sulfur and lithium sources after all mods have loaded. New setups can share those ores with Base Electric without adding extra veins. Existing worlds keep their choices and existing chunks stay as they are.

- Keep existing provider settings and vanilla ore choices when importing old configs.

- Support exact ore host variants and preserve native Mesa gold when vanilla ore management is off.
- Make the Austrian German translation selectable and give Pirate Speak its own menu and guide text.

Version 4.1.7.110021

* Keep completed retrogen marked through later saves and restarts, even while
  retrogen is off. Do not mark chunks with a revision they have not processed.

* Add loaded-chunk ore surveys, JSON/CSV reports, chunk details and rule
  explanations. Keep read-only diagnostics independent of generation settings.
* Restore terrain clearing with permission checks, a preview, a verified
  backup and checked undo. Keep ores, fluid deposits and unknown blocks safe.
  Show short previews with clickable confirmation, cancellation and undo links.

* Keep saved ore settings when a provider renames a recognised rule. Add the
  matching modern rule as a disabled alternative rather than another ore pass.

* Add provider/profile declarations and compiled natural rock formations.
  Use the same deterministic, chunk-local geometry for early terrain placement
  and geology prediction, with read-only formation and parent-material queries.
* Preserve caves, fluids, structures, other ores and existing chunks. Existing
  worlds without formation definitions keep that absence in later terrain too.
* Let realism templates tune untouched packaged formations while preserving
  authored, disabled, removed and authoritative external definitions.
* Keep native granite/diorite/andesite patches from cutting the expanded
  formation rocks differently according to chunk population order, without
  changing normal metal-ore hosts or older profiles.
* Preserve natural formation rock in vanilla lava-lake rims regardless of
  neighbouring chunk order. Keep native lake shapes, fluid cavities and random
  draws unchanged in normal, Amplified, Large Biomes and Customized worlds;
  leave older profiles and custom generators alone.

Version 4.1.6.110021

* Fix duplicate ore generation when an OreSpawn 1 world is moved without its
  converted provider file. Keep imported rules and saved choices, and back
  up the profile before removing a duplicate. Leave edited rules for review.
* Pick the default sulfur and lithium sources after all mods have loaded.
  New setups can share those ores with Base Electric without adding extra
  veins. Existing worlds keep their choices and existing chunks stay as they are.

Version 4.1.5.110021

* Apply the normal gold-generation controls to Mesa's extra gold pass too.
  Keep custom channels, imported settings and existing chunks unchanged.

Version 4.1.4.110021

* Let Java providers select an exact legacy host variant, such as plain stone
  without granite. Keep existing block selectors and placement behaviour.
* Reject invalid exact-host weights without leaving a partly configured host.

Version 4.1.3.110021

* Apply hybrid and replacement background limits to imported built-in ore
  patterns, just as for ordinary native rules. Keep explicit channels and
  third-party deposit patterns independent.
* Retain older Ore Sources selections under their saved pattern names without
  rewriting imported settings or regenerating existing chunks.
* Show imported placement choices in the editor without duplicate old-channel
  rows. Distinguish an inactive source from a missing mod, and keep custom
  channels and saved choices intact.
* Keep the empty Ore Sources message inside its pane in smaller windows.

Version 4.1.2.110021

* Respect Manage Vanilla Ores for imported OS1/OS3 rules. With it off, leave
  vanilla ore generation alone and keep those rules saved but inactive.
* With vanilla management on, use the imported placement settings without
  adding a second Minecraft or OreSpawn default pass. Keep saved settings,
  dimension limits and existing chunks unchanged.

Version 4.1.1.110021

* Keep existing provider settings when importing older OS1 or OS3 files for
  the first time, instead of replacing them with the older settings.
* Describe preserved settings as retained rather than verified in the upgrade
  report. Invalid files are still checked by the normal provider loader.

releases.notes:
Version 4.1.7.113021

* Add surveys, chunk reports and rule explanations for checking a modpack's
  generated terrain. Restore clearchunk with clickable previews, verified
  backups and checked undo.
* Keep retrogen completion markers through normal saves and server restarts,
  including when retrogen is switched off.
  Recover chunk bookkeeping through Forge 1.13's capability persistence, where
  the usual chunk-data load event is missing.
* Add optional natural rock formations, shared placement/sampling APIs and
  provider controls for background ore generation. Existing worlds keep their
  saved geology and generation choices.
* Let providers keep new structural defaults out of existing worlds, and let
  templates preserve edited formation settings.
* Replace ordinary Overworld fluid overrides after native terrain generation,
  preserving caves, later lakes and springs. Keep the compatibility path for
  fluids with different lighting properties.
  Keep native water-dependent decoration, including swamp trees, ice and
  aquatic plants, working with the substituted fluid.
* Rebuild release checksums when a release jar changes.
* Keep test fixtures compatible with Eclipse's Java 8 access restrictions.
* Keep native stone-patch suppression working when vanilla ore management
  wraps the same feature list.
* Avoid repeated chunk lookups and temporary arrays in ore and rock selection.
* Keep ore exposure checks inside the available generation region, fixing a
  chunk-boundary crash when generating ores with air-exposure rules.
* Keep saved ore settings when a provider renames a recognised rule. Add the
  matching modern rule as a disabled alternative rather than another ore pass.

Version 4.1.6.113021

* Leave vanilla ores to Minecraft when Manage Vanilla Ores is off. When
  it is on, an imported rule takes over without an extra copy of the ore.
* Keep saved Ore Sources choices for imported patterns. Built-in patterns
  share the standard channel for new choices; custom channels stay separate.
* Show vanilla ores in Ore Sources before creating a world, even when Manage
  Vanilla Ores is off.
* Keep imported provider rules when opening a saved world. Back up the
  profile before removing an untouched duplicate; keep edited rules for review.
* Choose sulfur and lithium defaults after mods have loaded, including Base
  Electric. Existing worlds keep their choices.
* Fix the Austrian German language ID and add Pirate Speak menu and guide text.

Version 4.1.0.113021

* Fix managed Nether quartz hosts on Forge 1.13.2, including saved profiles
  that refer to the absent forge:netherrack tag. Existing chunks stay untouched.
  New Nether ore and fluid-deposit rules also use the installed netherrack block.
* Add a directory for loaded provider mods and optional add-on settings screens.
* Group OreSpawn-managed ores by exact block tags. Balanced, Single, Custom,
  and Keep Original policies keep one placement budget per channel without
  changing existing worlds' saved behaviour.
* Add a biome directory with exact new-terrain replacement, palette settings,
  and dimension-wide materials controls. Existing chunks are never rewritten.
* Preserve missing-mod settings and dormant imported Ore Dictionary aliases.
  Provider, global, and world schemas are now 5, 8, and 7; API major remains 1.
* Keep the 4.0.16 Forge 1.13-specific behaviour: this target has neither
  three-dimensional biome-cell attribution nor a server-side GameTest harness.

Version 4.0.14.113021

* Convert exposed one-layer vanilla Snow from the first free cell immediately
  above Minecraft's motion-blocking surface when a dimension supplies a custom
  snow material.
* Retain the existing surface Ice conversion and leave buried or authored Snow
  and Ice unchanged.

Version 4.0.13.113021

* Give the public ore-dimension builder the exact biome include/exclude and
  biome-dictionary filter support already available in provider JSON.

* Keep biome and ore-list text visible with Minecraft's ARGB renderer.
* Move Help & Guide beside Recommended Defaults and fit both main menus above the footer.
* Reject invalid geome IDs without changing their spelling.
* Recognise inline vanilla ore features without changing mixed or unknown outputs.
* Release ore wrappers when a server stops and keep their shared biome ordering.
* Add shared-ore Eclipse profiles and real Nether fresh/reload checks.

* Add the mod directory, material-group ore controls, and built-in MMD conflict defaults.
* Add exact new-terrain biome replacement and dimension-wide material controls.
* Preserve old profiles and missing-mod settings when upgrading schemas to 5, 8, and 7.
* Split the build into smaller commented scripts and normalize tracked text to LF.

* Port the accepted Forge 26.2 implementation to Minecraft 26.3 and Forge
  66.0.0.
* Adapt OreSpawn's runtime world-generation features, feature gates, biome
  resolvers, and spring-host compatibility to Minecraft 26.3's immutable
  feature model while preserving generation stages and profile behaviour.
* Preserve one shared wrapper identity for each vanilla spring feature across
  biomes so decoration seeds and fixed-seed coordinates remain unchanged while
  OreSpawn geology blocks are accepted as additional spring hosts.
* Use ordinary chunk writes for fluid deposits so Minecraft 26.3 performs its
  required fluid bookkeeping.
* Requalify the sealed Mavenizer fixture for Forge 66 as an explicit zero-rule
  target.

mods.name: MMD OreSpawn
mods.description: Configurable, provider-driven terrain, ore, and deposit generation.

releases.notes:
Version 4.1.1.121012

* Use each dimension's actual height for rock strata, including deeper and
  taller worlds supplied by other mods or datapacks.
* Keep native rock where no configured rock is eligible, rather than replacing
  it with stone. Preserve saved ranges and leave existing chunks untouched.
* Allow rock height settings outside the vanilla range and explain how rock
  weights differ from a geome's family weights.

Version 4.1.0.121012

* Keep imported vanilla ore settings inactive while Manage Vanilla Ores is off.
  When it is on, use the imported settings without a second default ore pass.
* Treat imported built-in patterns as ordinary veins while retaining saved
  placement choices and independent custom channels.
* Show inactive sources separately from missing mods, without rewriting saved
  rules or choices just to display them.
* Put Help & Guide beside Recommended Defaults and fit the world-creation tab
  above the footer in smaller windows.
* Reject invalid geome names instead of silently changing their spelling.
* Recognise inline vanilla ore features and release their wrappers when a
  server stops, while preserving shared feature identities across biomes.
* Add an isolated shared-ore client profile and real Nether fresh/reload checks.
* Use Minecraft Mod Development as the jar vendor.
* Keep generated Javadoc artwork and license notices identical on Windows and Linux.

* Add provider extensions, a mod directory, Ore Sources and built-in MMD conflict defaults.
* Add the biome directory, exact new-terrain replacements and dimension material controls.
* Keep existing worlds' ore rules while starting new shared-tag MMD groups Balanced.
* Split the NeoGradle build into smaller scripts and keep tracked text in LF format.

Version 4.0.16.121012

* Leave benchmark shutdown to the GameTest harness when a benchmark is run
  through Minecraft's GameTest server, preventing a null test-tracker crash and
  allowing the harness to report its real test result.
* Ordinary dedicated benchmark servers still stop automatically when requested.

Version 4.0.15.121012

* Classify generated geology and public geology samples through the same
  stable quart-biome cell at three-dimensional biome boundaries.
* Keep ore family-host filters and sampler predictions consistent when later
  surface features alter the final heightmap by a small amount.
* Existing chunks, profiles, API signatures, and schemas are unchanged.

Version 4.0.14.121012

* Convert naturally exposed one-layer Snow at the first free block above the
  motion-blocking surface while retaining the existing Snow and Ice scan.
* Preserve buried or authored Snow and Ice, unconfigured dimensions, fluids,
  bedrock, block entities, profiles, schemas, and existing chunks.

Version 4.0.13.121012

* Give the public ore-dimension builder the exact biome include/exclude and
  biome-dictionary filter support already available in provider JSON.
* Accept valid namespaced geome IDs in both creation-editor validation paths
  while preserving legacy unnamespaced geome keys.
* API major 1, schemas, existing profiles, generated chunks, and worldgen
  behaviour are unchanged.

Version 4.0.12.121012

* Classify public geology samples at the same highest occupied block used by
  chunk geology generation, rather than the first free block above it.
* Keep public sampler predictions consistent with generated rock at vertical
  biome seams without changing existing chunks, profiles, or generation.

Version 4.0.11.121012

* Preserve biome-dictionary geome weights when a data-driven biome is reached
  through its stable registry key rather than the object baked at startup.
* Apply ore biome include and exclude filters by stable registry key so
  dynamic-registry biome instances with the same ID are treated consistently.
* Existing chunks and profile formats are unchanged; the corrections apply to
  generation in affected provider biomes.
